content:
Hi everyone! I'm Dmitry Vlasov, an independent researcher working on formal
mathematics for many years.

My background is on the Metamath side of the world. I develop Russell
(https://github.com/dmitry-vlasov/russell-flow), a
proof system built on the same theoretical basis as Metamath (assertions +
substitutions, no fixed calculus), with bidirectional translation to and from
Metamath. On top of it I built a general prover engine that works in this
calculus-agnostic setting, and recently a complete port of the Mizar verifier,
which reproduces the original byte-for-byte on the whole MML.

What brings me here: I care a lot about proofs a human can inspect in full
detail, down to every step. Lean proofs (proof terms, powerful tactics) are
kernel-checked but often hard to read as arguments. I'm exploring two ideas:

  1. A deep embedding of a Metamath-style substitution calculus in Lean 4, with a
    soundness bridge to native Lean propositions — in the spirit of mm0-lean,
    which as far as I can tell stayed a Lean 3 prototype.

  2. Tools to "unwrap" Lean proofs into an explicit step-by-step form, where each
    step is an application of a cited Mathlib lemma, and the substitution that
    instantiates the lemma is recovered by matching rather than written out —
    something like #explode, but with the rewrite plumbing cleaned up, so that
    every step reads as "this lemma, instantiated this way".

Before going further, I'd like to check: is anyone working on reviving the
Metamath↔Lean direction in Lean 4, or on readable/structured output for
automation (an isar_proofs-style reconstruction)? I'd be glad to join forces
rather than duplicate work.

Happy to be here!
This might be a question for @Mario Carneiro ?
I'm not sure if it helps your goal, but he helped me formalize this: https://github.com/pthomas505/meta_metamath_zero_lean
